findings.pdf_says: Figure E.8 is a three-column layout: left column (Physical Top of Form / Logical Top of Form / Logical Bottom of Form / Physical Bottom of Form), middle column 'PAGE clause phrases' (Heading, First Detail, Last Control Heading, Last Detail, Footing, Page Limit), right column 'Report content' (e.g. 'Heading' row: 'the first line of the report or page heading' / '<(first page only) report header lines>' / '<page heading lines>'; 'Footing' row: 'last line of Control footing or first line of a report or page footing' / '<page footing lines.' / '<(last page only) report footing lines>').

findings.why_it_matters: The page-layout figure's three columns are flattened and interleaved: the form-position labels are fused with the PAGE clause phrase names ('Logical Top Heading', 'Logical Page Limit'), a two-row table splits 'Logical Top of Form' across rows, and the phrase names run into their content text, so a reader cannot tell which report content belongs to which PAGE phrase or form position. Informative annex E figure; no text is lost but the column association is.
